title: Union-find and connectivity

objectives.text: Maintain a partition with representative equality, root sizes and successful-merge component counts.
Explain how path compression changes representation without changing connectivity, and distinguish amortized bounds from per-call latency.
Parse signed hundredths exactly and filter every edge with strict comparison.
Return all components including isolates with canonical member/group ordering.
Prove safe acceptance by a light-cut-edge exchange.
Handle self/parallel edges,disconnected/singleton output and wide total cost.

blocks.markdown: A disjoint-set structure maintains a partition of known elements into non-overlapping sets. Initially IDs 0 through n-1 each form a singleton. find(x) returns a representative of the set containing x; union(a,b) merges the two sets if different. The representative is an implementation choice and can change after a merge. It is not automatically the smallest ID, first arrival, legal owner or business label. Compare representatives for equality, not a particular numeric value unless that is a separate maintained contract.

Represent each set by a rooted parent tree with parent[root]=root. Following parents reaches its representative. Only root size entries are authoritative; a size stored at a former root may be stale after attachment. Before merging, find both roots. If equal, return False and do not decrement the component count. Otherwise attach the smaller tree below the larger root, add sizes at the surviving root and decrement the number of components once.

blocks.caption: Expected output: True, True, False, True, 3, 3 on separate lines. Two successful merges reduce five components to three; the repeated connection changes no partition. All endpoint checks reject bool, negative and out-of-range IDs. find may mutate parent pointers by compression even though it returns the same connectivity information.

blocks.markdown: The first pass in find reaches the root. The second pass rewires every visited non-root vertex directly to that root while remembering the old next pointer. It changes the internal parent forest, not which elements are in the same set. A parent chain is not a path of original graph edges: union can connect representatives that were not the exact input edge endpoints. Do not use DSU parents to reconstruct a shortest graph route.

blocks.source:
# A valid parent forest before a find on element3.
parent = [0, 0, 1, 2]
root = 3
while parent[root] != root:
    root = parent[root]
vertex = 3
while parent[vertex] != vertex:
    following = parent[vertex]
    parent[vertex] = root
    vertex = following
print(root)
print(parent)
blocks.caption: Expected output: 0, then [0, 0, 0, 0]. Elements 3, 2 and 1 still belong to the same set as before; the paths are simply shorter. This isolated valid-forest trace illustrates compression; it is not a claim that the shown chain was produced by the union-by-size policy.

blocks.markdown: Without compression, attaching the smaller tree below the larger means a vertex whose depth increases joins a component at least twice as large as before. Its depth can therefore increase at most floor(log2(n)) times before the component contains all n elements. Compression only shortens these paths. Combining union by size/rank and compression gives a very slowly growing inverse-Ackermann amortized bound across a sequence of operations. That advanced bound is cited, not proved here; it is not a promise that every operation takes identical constant time or meets a production latency target.

For an undirected network with additions only, each new edge can union its endpoints. A successful merge joins two previously disconnected components; an edge whose endpoints already share a representative is redundant for connectivity. With parallel edges or self-loops it may still be a distinct business event. DSU does not preserve the full edge log. If deletions can split components, ordinary DSU cannot undo them correctly just by changing one parent pointer.

This implementation is not a rollback or persistent DSU, a directed strong-connectivity algorithm, a path-distance index or an authenticated identity registry. Concurrent mutations need their own synchronization contract. A snapshot of parent arrays is also representation-specific; stable external component labels require a declared mapping. Keep the original event history separately when replay or audits require it.

Independent transfer: compare DSU connectivity and component sizes to a plain set-partition oracle after each small merge. Include repeated unions, self-unions, isolated elements and invalid endpoints. Check that root sizes sum to n and that the component counter equals the number of distinct representatives. Snapshot before a find and confirm that compression can change parents while preserving every pairwise connectivity answer. Explain why deleting an input edge is not supported by this interface.

Reference: [Disjoint Set Union](https://cp-algorithms.com/data_structures/disjoint_set_union.html) for parent forests, union by size and compression. The logarithmic depth argument is explained here; the inverse-Ackermann sequence bound is an externally established theorem, not a learner proof completed by running this example. All network semantics are synthetic.

Exact link predicate

Source: n1..100000,m0..200000,assets0..n-1. The CURRENT supplied parser passes theta and rho as two-decimal STRINGS, not floats. rho is in[-1.00,1.00]. Form magnitude100*whole+fractional,then apply the sign to the entire magnitude. Thus-0.20is-20,-0.00is0. Compare rho>theta: equality is NOT linked. This parses guaranteed two-decimal text,not arbitrary numeric notation.

DSU invariant after filtering

After each edge prefix,DSU sets are precisely components of accepted links from that prefix. A rejected line changes nothing;an accepted line unions its endpoints. Duplicate pairs are evaluated per line:a rejected observation does not cancel a later accepted one. Already-connected/reverse links are idempotent. Connectivity is transitive even if the endpoint pair itself has a low observed correlation. The complete block includes iterative path compression and union by size from the core invariant.

Roots are not output order

Union by size chooses structural representatives,not minimum member IDs. Visit EVERY vertex ascending,including isolates,find its final root and append it to that bucket. Members are then increasing. Sort buckets by their first member,not root ID. Return count line then space-joined members. With theta0.50,accept0-1at0.80and1-2at0.55,reject3-4at0.50and0-2at-0.20:output triple0,1,2then singleton3then4.

Work and independent transfer

DSU O(n)storage and amortized inverse-Ackermann work per operation by the cited theorem,not a proof of constant worst-case latency. Group sorting adds O(k log k),input/output storage O(n+m),formatting proportional to emitted digits. Independently construct the accepted graph with exact rational predicates and flood components. Include equality,signedzero,negative thresholds,duplicates,isolates and maximum dimensions. These are connectivity clusters,not pairwise-all-correlated groups or certified risk models.

Forest invariant

Sort a COPY of edges by weight ascending. DSU components equal components of selected forest. Same-root endpoints mean cycle/self-link:skip. Different roots:union,add weight,increment selected. Each acceptance reduces component count1. n-1accepted means spanning tree. Ties may change chosen edges,not minimum total. Parallel edges compete normally,not summed together.

Cut exchange proof

For connected input,maintain chosen forest Acontained in SOME MST. Next accepted e crosses cut Sdefined by one current component;no Aedge crosses. e is lightest crossing:an earlier crossing edge would have joined components already. If MST Tcontaining Aomits e,adding ecreates one cycle with another crossing edge fnotinA. Since w(e)<=w(f),replace fby e:still spanning tree,no greater cost,and preserves A. Thus some MST contains A+e. Ties allowed;not every MST must contain every light edge.

summary: Maintain partition invariants, root-only sizes and successful-merge counts. Compression changes representation, not connectivity. Ordinary DSU handles merges, not arbitrary deletions, path reconstruction or directed strong components. Extension: exact threshold clusters. Extension: kruskal safe forest.
